parts.problem_md:
![Circle with three points on its circumference labelled A, B and Q. A line segment inside the circle joins points A and B.  Another line segment, with endpoints V and W, touches the circle at Q. The part of the circle on one side of line AB is shaded in. "Not to scale" is noted in text.](assets/001-circle-with-three-points-on-its-circumference-la.png)

Points $A$ and $B$ lie on the circle.
A region has been shaded between line $AB$ and the circumference of the circle.

The area of the circle is 76.4 cm<sup>2</sup>.

Calculate the radius of the circle.

.......................................... cm
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> The formula for the area, $A$, of a circle is given on the list of formulas in the exam paper:
> 
> $A=πr^{2}$
> 
> - where $r$ is the radius

Here you know the area, and you want to know the radius

Start by putting the given area into the formula in place of $A$

$76.4=πr^{2}$

Now you need to solve that for $r$

- First divide both sides by $π$, to get rid of the $π$ on the right-hand side

$\frac{76.4}{π}=r^{2}$

**[M1]**

- You can use your calculator to work out the value of that

$r^{2}=24.318875...$

- To find the value of $r$, take the square root of that

  - Use your calculator's memory, or the Ans key, to make sure you are taking the square root of that exact value

$r=\sqrt{24.318875...}=4.931417...$

Round to a suitable degree of accuracy

- In general you should round to 3 significant figures, unless the question specifies otherwise
- The fourth significant figure is a '1'

  - which tells you not to change the third significant figure '3'

**Final answer:** **4.93 cm (3 s.f.)**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For $r^{2}=\frac{76.4}{π}$ or a correct subsequent step in the solution process.
> 
> **A1**: For 4.93 or 4.931 to 4.932.

parts.problem_md:
The diameter of a different circle is 38 mm.

Calculate the circumference of this circle.
Give your answer in centimetres.

.......................................... cm
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> The formula for the circumference, $C$, of a circle is given on the list of formulas in the exam paper:
> 
> $C=2πr$
> 
> - where $r$ is the radius
> 
> But be careful in this question, as you are given the diameter and not the radius!

Start by finding the radius

- The radius is half the diameter

$r=\frac{38}{2}=19\mathrm{mm}$

Put that into the formula

$C=2\timesπ\times19$

**[M1]**

- and use your calculator to work out the value

$C=119.380520...$

**[B1]**

But that figure is in millimetres

- because the radius was in millimetres

To convert to centimetres, divide that by 10

- because there are 10 mm in 1 cm

$119.380520...\div10=11.9380520...$

Round to a suitable degree of accuracy

- In general you should round to 3 significant figures, unless the question specifies otherwise
- The fourth significant figure is a '3'

  - which tells you not to change the third significant figure '9'

**Final answer:** **11.9 cm (3 s.f.)**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For $C=2\timesπ\times19$ or equivalent, e.g. $C=2\timesπ\times1.9$ if the conversion to cm has been made before this.
> 
> **B1**: For 119 or 119.3 to 119.4; or for 11.938... if the conversion to cm has been made before this.
> 
> **A1**: For 11.9 or 11.93 to 11.94.

parts.problem_md:
![q10e-058032-march2019-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/002-q10e-058032-march2019-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

This shape is drawn using two semicircles that have the same centre.

The large semicircle has radius 7 cm.

The small semicircle has radius 3 cm.

Calculate the area of the shape.

.............................. cm<sup>2</sup>
parts.solution_md:
> *The area of a semicircle is calculated using the formula: *$A=\frac{π\timesr^{2}}{2}$* where *$r$* is the radius of the circle.*

> *Calculate the area of the larger semicircle with *$r=7cm$

$A=\frac{π\times7^{2}}{2}=24.5π$

> *Calculate the area of the smaller semicircle with *$r=3cm$

$A=\frac{π\times3^{2}}{2}=4.5π$

$24.5π$** or **$4.5π$** seen** **[1]**

> *Subtract the area of the smaller semicircle from the larger semicircle to determine the area of the shaded region*

$24.5π-4.5π$

**[1]**

$=20π=62.83185307$

> *Round to 3 significant figures*

**62.8 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** [1] **

**Or 62.83 to 62.84**

equations.alt: A equals fraction numerator straight pi cross times r squared over denominator 2 end fraction
A equals fraction numerator straight pi cross times 7 squared over denominator 2 end fraction equals 24.5 straight pi
A equals fraction numerator straight pi cross times 3 squared over denominator 2 end fraction equals 4.5 straight pi

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a rectangle and two semicircles with diameters $AC$ and $BD$. 
This diagram is a scale drawing of a running track. $AC=BD=60m\,AB=CD=120m$

![q9-058032-march2019-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/003-q9-058032-march2019-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

i) Complete the statement.

1 centimetre represents ............................ metres.

[2]

ii) Work out the total length of the running track in metres.

............................. m [3]

iii) Shreva walks at 1.4m/s.

Work out how long it will take her to walk once around the track. Give your answer in minutes and seconds, correct to the nearest second.

.................... minutes .................... seconds [3]
parts.solution_md:
i) *Using a ruler, measure the distance of *$CD$

$8\mathrm{cm}$

**[1]**

> *Divide the actual size by the measured length to determine the scale factor*

$120\div8=15m$

*1 centimetre represents **15 **metres***. [1]**

ii) *The circumference of a circle is calculated using the formula *$C=πd$*. *
*As the two parts of the running track between *$AC$* and *$BD$* are two identical semicircles, these create one full circle.*

> *Determine the circumference of this circle where *$d=60m$

$C=π\times60=188.4955592$

**[1]**

> *Add this distance to the two equivalent distances of *$CD$* and *$AB$

$120+120+188.4955592=428.4955592$

**[1]**

> *Round to 3 significant figures*

$428m$ **[1] **

**Or 428.4 or 428.5, or 428.49 to 428.52**

iii) *Substitute the values of *$D=428.5m$* and *$S=1.4m/s$* into the formula:*

> *Time = *$\frac{\mathrm{Distance}}{\mathrm{Speed}}$

$T=\frac{428.5}{1.4}=306.0714286$* seconds*

**[1]**

> *As *$300$* minutes is equivalent to *$5$* minutes*

$60\times5=300$* seconds*

**[1]**

> *the time in minutes and seconds is*

$5$** ****minutes **$6$** seconds** **[1]**

A B space equals space C D space equals space 120 straight m
120 divided by 8 equals 15 space straight m
C equals straight pi cross times 60 equals 188.4955592

parts.problem_md:
![q8b-058031-mayjune2019-cie-igcse-maths-core](assets/004-q8b-058031-mayjune2019-cie-igcse-maths-core.png)

Points $P,Q$ and $R$ are on the circumference of a semicircle, centre $O$ and radius 8 cm. 
Angle $POQ$ = 90°.

Calculate the shaded area.

.........................................cm<sup>2</sup>
parts.solution_md:
> *The area of a semicircle is half the area of a circle. *

> *Substitute known values into the formula *$A=\frac{πr^{2}}{2}$* where *$r$* is the radius of the full circle*

$A=\frac{π\times8^{2}}{2}$

**[1]**

$=32π$

**[1]**

> *The area of a triangle is calculated using the formula *$A=\frac{b\timesh}{2}$* where *$b$* is the base and *$h$* is the perpendicular height.*

> *Substitute the known values into the formula and evaluate*

$A = \frac{( 8 \times 2 ) \times 8}{2}$

**[1]**

$=64$

**[1]**

> *Subtract the area of the triangle from the area of the semicircle to determine the area of the shaded region*

$32π-64$

$=36.53096491$

**36.5 cm**<sup>**2**</sup>** (3sf)**** [1]**

parts.solution_md:

$\begin{gathered} \text{Angle} O B C & = 180 - 140 \\ = 40^{\circ} \end{gathered}$

**[1]**

> *Angle **OBC** = angle **FOH **(**alternate **angles are equal). *

$40^{\circ}$* ***[1]**

(iii) *Write *$40^{\circ}$* (angle **FOH**) as a fraction of *$360^{\circ}$* (degrees in a full circle) and multiply by the circumference of the circle, *$22π$*.  *

$\frac{40}{360}\times22π=7.67944...$

**7.68 cm** **[1]**

> *(Because it is a square inside the circle, the dashed-line diagonals will meet at right angles at point **O**.)  *

$\frac{1}{2}\times6\times6=18$

$113.0973...-72=41.0973...$

* ***[1]**

> *Round to 3 significant figures. *

**41.1 cm**<sup>**2**</sup> **[1]**
